### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2c93a85-c8a8-4118-b917-15d6fd4f6114

Here is the error message:

```text
Error executing vim.schedule lua callback: ...o/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1374: Invalid 'col': out of range
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'nvim_buf_set_extmark'
        ...o/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1374: in function 'apply_tracked_text_edits'
        ...o/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1351: in function <...o/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim/lua/mini/completion.lua:1317>
```

In the above video, I tested:

1. on the [latest commit](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/commit/e7538b549361c9ac8416a07b0223ce03c508bfe7), it raises the above error.
2. on the commit before [ca73354](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/commit/ca7335433ceb16d7eef523338276f23d6aad17f5), everything works fine.
3. on the commit before [5d938b3](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/commit/5d938b3a078a7eeae23ba9f04f180066ab8bd9ef), additonal `x` characters are prepended to the inserted snippet, as described in #1948.

### Reproduction

The minimal reproducing configuration:

<details>
<summary>Instructions to install mini.nvim</summary>

```lua
-- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

-- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
require('mini.deps').setup()

-- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
-- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
```

</details>

```lua
require('mini.completion').setup()

-- Install with:
-- ```sh
-- curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- --default-toolchain none -y
-- rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rust-analyzer
-- ```
-- For more information see <https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install>.
vim.lsp.config('rust_analyzer', {
  cmd = { 'rust-analyzer' },
  filetypes = { 'rust' },
  settings = {},
})
vim.o.signcolumn = 'yes'
vim.lsp.enable('rust_analyzer')
```

The file I was editing and steps to reproduce:

```rust
// src/main.rs


struct Test(_);
//          ^ 1. Type "Phan"
//            2. Select the first candidate (should be "PhantomData<...>")
//            3. Error occurs

fn main() {}
```

rust-analyzer requires additional files to work properly, and I already uploaded them [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/compare/e7538b549361c9ac8416a07b0223ce03c508bfe7...loichyan:mini.nvim:issue/text-edit-error).

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

TL;DR: I believe this is an issue with `rust_analyzer` not behaving according to LSP specification. It updates item's `textEdit` property as a result of `completionItem/resolve` request, which it should not do.

Closing as not an issue with 'mini.completion', because it (rightfully) assumes that item's `textEdit` is final when returned as a result of initial `textDocument/completion` request.

---

I initially could not reproduce this with my main setup, but could indeed reproduce with the repro steps. The first assumed reason this happened is because `rust_analyzer` returns different shapes of completion candidates in two setups:
- In my setup it returned candidates with `textEdit` in the [`InsertReplaceEdit`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#insertReplaceEdit) form.
- In repro setup it returned `textEdit` in the [`textEdit`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textEdit) form.

This happened because [setting client capabilities](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/e7538b549361c9ac8416a07b0223ce03c508bfe7/doc/mini-completion.txt#L139-L140) is probably a good idea now with 'mini.completion'. Adding a line `vim.lsp.config('*', { capabilities = MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities() })` after `require('mini.completion').setup()` in repro 'init.lua' removes the error.

The specific capability that affects whether there is an error or not turned out to be `textDocument.completion.completionItem.insertReplaceSupport = true` (it is `false` by default), which explains different returned `textEdit` shape, but doesn't explain the error.

So after digging a bit deeper, turns out in both cases `rust_analyzer` updates candidate's `textEdit` during `completionItem/resolve` request (which is [done when trying to compute item's info](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/e7538b549361c9ac8416a07b0223ce03c508bfe7/doc/mini-completion.txt#L32-L33)) and uses the current buffer text as reference. When selecting an item with `<C-n>`, item's `word` is inserted in buffer which makes `rust_analyzer` assume that it was typed as whole which later contradicts with how 'mini.completion' sets extmarks. By the way, selecting an item with `<Down>` doesn't insert its `word` and there is no error as a result. There is also no error if item is accepted while info window didn't finish (like with higher delay).

Here is a part of LSP spec that describes important `completionItem/resolve` behavior (emphasis mine):

> Since 3.16.0 the client can signal that it can resolve more properties lazily. This is done using the `completionItem#resolveSupport` client capability which lists all properties that can be filled in during a ‘completionItem/resolve’ request. All other properties (usually `sortText`, `filterText`, `insertText` and `textEdit`) must be provided in the [`textDocument/completion`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_completion) response and **must not be changed during resolve**.

In both cases (with 'mini.completion' and with default LSP client capabilities) `textEdit` is not part of `textDocument.completion.completionItem.resolveSupport` properties, hence `rust_analyzer` does things wrong here.

In particular, after typing `Ph` and selecting with `<C-n>`, here is what `rust_analyzer` returns as a value of `textEdit`:

<details><summary>Different values of `textEdit`</summary>

- With `textDocument.completion.completionItem.insertReplaceSupport = true`:
    - `textDocument/completion`:

        ```
        insert = {
          start = { line = 2, character = 12 },
          ["end"] = { line = 2, character = 14 },
        },
        newText = "PhantomData<$0>",
        replace = {
          start = { line = 2 character = 12 },
          ["end"] = { line = 2 character = 14 },
        }
        ```

    - `completionItem/resolve`:

        ```
        insert = {
          start = { line = 2 character = 12 },
          ["end"] = { line = 2 character = 14 },
        },
        newText = "PhantomData<$0>",
        replace = {
          start = { line = 2 character = 12 },
          ["end"] = { line = 2 character = 23 },
        }
        ```
- With `textDocument.completion.completionItem.insertReplaceSupport = true`:
    - `textDocument/completion`:

        ```
        newText = "PhantomData<$0>",
        range = {
          start = { line = 2, character = 12 },
          ["end"] = { line = 2, character = 14 },
        }
        ```

    - `completionItem/resolve`:

        ```
        newText = "PhantomData<$0>",
        range = {
          start = { character = 12, line = 2 },
          ["end"] = { line = 2, character = 23 },
        }
        ```

</details>

So the final answer to the mystery is that it just so happens that 'mini.completion' uses `insert` part to compute item's edit range (which is used when setting extmark when there is an error) and it seems to not change in `completionItem/resolve`

---

And this is yet another example of why I don't like working with LSP: an answer to just the question of whether it is an issue on 'mini.completion' side, LSP server, or Neovim takes *a lot* of effort.

Wow, it's really tricky! Thanks for your elaboration! ❤️

> Adding a line vim.lsp.config('*', { capabilities = MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities() }) after require('mini.completion').setup() in repro 'init.lua' removes the error.

I did have this line in my own configurations, but I just realized that I was using [rustaceanvim](https://github.com/mrcjkb/rustaceanvim), which defines its own way to handle LSP configurations and doesn't seem to respect the configured capabilities. After explicitly telling it about mini.completion's capabilities, this issue was resolved. Sorry for bothering!
